findings.title: Parallel repairs invalidate the compare timing
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:4969 measures one wall-clock Compare span, while line 5425 records every repair duration separately; phase_probe.rs:443 subtracts their sum. After mod.rs:5241 parallelizes repairs, overlapping durations can exceed wall time, making saturating_sub report Compare as zero and hide real stat/metadata cost on repair-heavy runs.

findings.title: Blocking destination I/O monopolizes the shared Rayon pool
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:5241 runs blocking SMB metadata calls on Rayon's global CPU pool. The concurrent apply path uses that same pool for tar-shard writes at remote/transfer/sink.rs:1361 and 1381, and daemon sessions share it too. A slow diff can therefore stall apply or unrelated transfers; the recorded 24x per-call latency inflation reinforces this risk. Use an explicitly bounded destination-I/O executor and benchmark copying plus concurrent remote sessions.

findings.title: The parallel map makes errors and attribute repairs schedule-dependent
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:5240-5260 performs filesystem mutations inside a fallible parallel map. Rayon does not deterministically return the first of multiple errors, contrary to line 5235, and duplicate manifest paths are deduplicated only afterward at lines 4975 and 5093, so two closures can repair the same destination concurrently. Reject/deduplicate paths before parallel work or keep verdict computation pure and apply ordered mutations afterward.

findings.title: The added parallel-diff test does not guard parallelism
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/tests/local_session.rs:1592 checks only the resulting file set. Replacing mod.rs:5241 into_par_iter with into_iter and removing the Rayon import left the intended test green (1 passed); after exact-byte restoration it remained green. The central 1.34x behavior can therefore disappear without this guard failing.
